How do I start using SubHub?

Complete setup and grant the Android access needed for your features. In Dom mode, open People and select a Sub. Open Contract to choose apps and configure features. For a session on this device, choose a duration on the local profile and tap Start session.\n\nThe Sub’s Overview shows their session, app time, and achievements. The Contract tab shows their current configuration.
What can the Dom and Sub do?

The Dom configures apps, feature settings, and session duration. The Sub can view their contract and use available actions. Use the header’s Unlock control with the Dom PIN or keyholder code to edit protected settings.\n\nKeyholder and device connections are in Settings. App Lock and the screen privacy filter protect access or visibility; neither grants Dom authorization.
How do sessions start and end?

In Dom mode, open the local profile, choose a duration, and tap Start session. The Dom can end an active session from the profile. A paired Sub’s profile can also offer End session when its current state is available; starting a session on a paired device is not available here. A timed session also ends at its deadline. The last duration and Random bounds remain selected after a session and when you reopen the app. Switching between Dom and Sub does not end an active session.\n\nAndroid can interrupt background access, and Screen Capture needs fresh Android approval for each session. Check the Sub’s Overview after restarting the device.
Which apps does SubHub affect?

In Dom mode, open People → the selected Sub → Contract. The Apps section shows the selection; use Add more to change it. This selection applies to Censor, Limits, Subliminal Messaging, and Popup Storm. All Apps includes eligible launchable apps installed later without changing the saved selection. Turn it off to use that selection again. Essential Android screens, keyboards, and SubHub itself are excluded where needed.\n\nSelecting apps does not enable a disabled feature. Set per-app allowances in Limits. Removing an app does not erase usage already counted toward today’s combined budget.
Which Android access do I need?

Accessibility supplies foreground-app changes and the live controls used by Limits. Display over other apps allows visible overlays. On Android 13 and newer, notification permission lets SubHub show its ongoing status. Use Android Access above to check permissions and open the Access Guide.\n\nScreen Capture and Censor Lab recording require separate Android approval. Hardcore requests Device Admin separately; ordinary censoring does not require it.
How does Censor work?

Open Censor from the selected Sub’s Contract. Choose Low, Medium, or High detection to enable it, or Off to disable it. Detection coverage and censor appearance are separate choices; changing the look does not change the detection level.\n\nCensor works on supported visible images and text in selected apps while a session is running. Secure windows and some Android surfaces cannot be captured. Censor photos & videos handles chosen files separately.
How do app limits work?

Limits has separate controls for per-app allowances and the combined daily budget. Enable either or both. There is no additional feature switch. If both apply, the smaller remaining allowance determines the available time.\n\nUsage resets at local midnight. When an applicable budget runs out, SubHub returns the covered app to the Android home screen. Limits needs Accessibility; Screen Capture alone cannot track and enforce foreground-app time.
How does Tribute work?

Open Tribute from the selected Sub’s Contract and enable the rules you want. Any enabled rule can run during a session; turning all rules off stops new rule-based tributes. There is no separate feature switch. Set prices, batching, correction time, and daily or weekly caps before starting.\n\nTributes are recorded locally until payment is authorized. Paid Pause has its own offer checkbox and price and can run independently. Turning off tribute rules does not remove existing history or unpaid amounts.
How do I connect PayPal?

Open Tribute from the selected Sub’s Contract, then open PayPal. Select Sandbox for testing or Live for real payments, then connect the matching PayPal REST app credentials. Live and Sandbox credentials and wallets are separate.\n\nA saved payer wallet requires PayPal Vault capability for the merchant app and the payer’s approval through PayPal. Linking a wallet does not charge it. Manual checkout requires the payer to approve payment. Check connection and wallet status on the PayPal tab before relying on a payment method.
What does Hardcore change?

Hardcore adds Android-supported friction to protected uninstall, data-clear, and settings paths while service is active. It uses Device Admin and Dom authorization for release. It does not make Android impossible to bypass. Keep the Dom PIN and a recovery path available.\n\nSaved-wallet automatic payment is a separate, explicit choice. It also requires an active service lock, Hardcore, applicable Tribute rules, and a verified saved wallet. PayPal may decline a payment or ask the payer to authorize again.
Atmosphere

Open Atmosphere from the selected Sub’s Contract to configure Subliminal Messaging and Popup Storm independently. Both use the configured app selection during a session. Popup Storm also has a safety stop.
How does Censor photos & videos handle originals?

Open Censor photos & videos from the Censor page to create censored copies of selected images or videos. Choose media and review the preview and output settings before exporting. An export uses the settings chosen when it starts, even if live settings change later.\n\nExports can continue in the background and show saved progress or results when you return. Original files remain unless you explicitly choose deletion. Review an exported copy before deleting an original.
Profiles

In Dom mode, open People and choose a Sub. Their profile shows the session and links to Contract, Stats, and Connection. Contract contains the selected apps and feature settings. Activity shows recorded app opens, triggered Tributes, and reached limits.\n\nThe Sub’s Overview shows their session, app time, and achievements; their Contract and Stats are available from the navigation bar. Dom authentication is required to edit protected settings. A paired Sub keeps applied settings while offline. Android permissions, local credentials, and payment authorization stay on the device.
Why is a feature not working?

Check that service is running, the app is included, the feature’s own controls are enabled, and Android access is granted. For Limits, check the applicable allowance. For Tribute, check the rule and caps. For Censor, check that detection is not Off.\n\nDiagnostics shows actual service and detector state, timing, and recent errors. Censor Lab lives inside Diagnostics. Both are available to the Sub; changing the diagnostics overlay requires Dom. Lab recording starts only after you approve Android screen capture. Stop remains available during recording. Review recordings before sharing: they may contain visible screen content. A permission being granted does not prove that the live service is connected.
What stays on this device?

Image and text detection run on this device. Ordinary screen snapshots are processed in memory rather than saved. Pairing shares the approved configuration, app catalog, service status, statistics, and recorded activity with the assigned device. Revoking a relationship stops further sharing. Payment credentials and local authentication remain on this device.\n\nCensor Lab saves a recording only after Android approval and does not record microphone audio. PayPal credentials and saved-wallet identifiers use Android Keystore protection; authorization, checkout, and risk data are sent to PayPal. Updates contact GitHub. Stable updates are the default; development updates are opt-in. Downloads require your tap and installation requires Android approval.
